root_idea.summary: The root has two closely related semantic orientations: worshipful purification and swift movement or striving.
root_idea.development: The movement branch denotes swimming, gliding, rapid travel, and active occupation; the worship branch develops into declaring God free from every imperfection, glorifying Him, and associated acts of prayer and devotion.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Presented under the singular active-participle citation form.
Presented under the singular active-participle citation form.

senses.definition: To swim, float, or glide swiftly along a course.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, the subject is celestial bodies moving through their orbits; the image is based on swimming or gliding through water or air.

senses.definition: To declare God free from every imperfection and to glorify, magnify, praise, or celebrate Him.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction may occur with or without a preposition and may include praise of God as an accompanying expression; it includes the glorification of God by human beings and by created things.
This is an explicitly attested Quranic interpretation of the verb, including prayer that may be obligatory or supererogatory; the broader devotional sense may include acts beyond formal prayer.

senses.definition: To make an exception by saying “if God wills.”
senses.usage_conditions: This conventional construction is explicitly applied to the Quranic passage concerning the owners of the garden who failed to qualify their oath.

senses.definition: One who glorifies or praises God; one engaged in tasbih.
senses.usage_conditions: The participle can describe worship expressed in word, deed, or intention, and applies in the Quran to those characterized by glorification.

senses.definition: One devoted to worship, including prayer.
senses.usage_conditions: In the account of Jonah, the expression is also interpreted as referring to those who pray; this is a reported interpretation within the broader devotional sense.

senses.definition: Swift swimming, gliding, or passage along a course.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic image includes movement through water, air, or the firmament and can be extended to the rapid, extended-foreleg running of a horse.

senses.definition: Active movement or occupation in going about one's affairs.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic daytime expression, the word is explained variously as freedom or scope for activity, coming and going, attending to one's affairs, or prolonged occupation in them.

senses.definition: An utterance declaring God far removed from every imperfection, impurity, false attribution, or evil; glory be to God.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in Quranic formulas of transcendence and repudiation, including responses to claims that God has a partner, child, equal, or other unsuitable attribute.

senses.definition: A glorification formula functioning as an exhortation to worship or pray.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic formula associated with entering evening and morning, the expression is interpreted either as declaring God's transcendence or as an injunction to perform prayer.

senses.definition: One that glides, swims, or speeds smoothly along.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic plural expression, the referents have been interpreted as ships, the souls of believers, angels, stars, or other beings that glide swiftly; the lexical sense is the common image of smooth rapid passage.

senses.definition: Glorifying God by declaring Him free from imperfection and praising Him.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic noun denotes the glorification of God, including the tasbih attributed to all created things even when its manner is not understood by human beings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To move swiftly, become distant, travel far, or spread over a distance; figuratively, of fame, to travel or become widespread.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Form I movement branch, including rapid travel through land and figurative extension from swimming.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go to and fro, become dispersed in the land, or busy oneself seeking a livelihood and managing affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the Form I verbal use of active occupation and pursuit of affairs, distinct from the nominal Quranic expression سَبْحٌ in the daytime.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sleep or a state of being still, quiet, or motionless.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as an extended use of the Form I verbal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a mirage, to glisten or flash.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative visual extension of movement or shimmering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dig or burrow into the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to the jerboa.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be profuse in speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic Form I use with speech as the domain of expansive movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To swim with another person; to compete or vie in swimming.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III reciprocal or interactive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone swim, whether in or upon the water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV causative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A garment made of skins; in a reported variant, skin shirts for boys.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal lexical item distinguished from سُبْحَةٌ with the vowel pattern of the devotional noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Beads strung on a thread for counting repeated praises of God.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term also denotes the devotional act counted with such beads.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Invocation, supplication, prayer, or supererogatory praise and prayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may refer especially to supererogatory prayer, including the prayer of the forenoon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The majesty, greatness, light, or splendour associated with God or His face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In expressions concerning the divine face, it can denote evidences of majesty, splendour, or beauty, and by extension a declaration of transcendence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Places of prostration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported use, possibly referring to prostrations in Quran recitation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece of cotton.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Prayer, especially supererogatory prayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The use arises from the glorification performed in prayer and is distinct from the primary meaning of verbal glorification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An expression of wonder or astonishment at a thing or person: how extraordinary or strange!
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later generalized use of the transcendence formula beyond its reference to God.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The self or one's own mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression for what is within one's own mind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Swimming or the art of swimming; specifically, moving across the surface of water without immersion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verbal noun or simple noun for the activity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An epithet of God meaning all-perfect, all-pure, all-glorious, and free from every evil or imperfection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also pronounced سَبُّوحٌ; often paired with قُدُّوسٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A swimmer; by intensive extension, a great or frequent swimmer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Active participle and intensive participial uses of Form I.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse that stretches its forelegs well while running; by substantivization, a horse of that kind and a name given to certain horses or a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional equine epithet derived from the image of swimming.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single act or utterance of tasbih.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural forms refer to multiple acts of glorification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place for swimming.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its plural is used for places of swimming.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A strong garment of the type called كِسَاء; according to another explanation, a wide one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized passive-participial epithet applied to a garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The forefinger, or index finger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: So called because it is raised in the gesture associated with declaring divine unity.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The horse-running image is included in the Quran-attested movement sense.
Editorial pointer about a meaning assigned elsewhere.
Proper-name usage, not an independent lexical branch.
Morphological and synonymic explanation covered by the Quranic subhan sense.

cautions: The Quranic expression سَابِحَاتِ has several reported referents—ships, believing souls, angels, or stars—while retaining the common sense of swift gliding.
The Quranic سَبْحًا in 73:7 has several closely related interpretations, including daytime freedom, coming and going, and occupation in one's affairs.
Prayer and the making of an exception are specialized Quranic constructions of سَبَّحَ; they should not be reduced to the ordinary English gloss “glorify.”
